interpretations: The mean of all pair averages is the unweighted mean across every (orderslink, acctscope) pair's average feerate, and each pair counts once regardless of how many fee rows it has
The mean of all pair averages is the global mean over all pairs, computed before the strictly-above filter and across all scopes together
The mean of all pair averages is computed separately within each account scope, so each pair is compared to its own scope's mean of pair averages
The mean of all pair averages is the mean of per-pair averages after dropping pairs whose average is null (pairs where every feerate is missing)
The mean is the average of all individual fee rates (row-level) rather than the average of the pair averages
Fees without a matching order, or orders without a matching user, are dropped (inner joins), and fees with null feerate are ignored in the averages but the fee row still counts toward the join
Fees with null feerate are excluded before grouping, so pairs with only null feerates do not appear at all
Ranking uses RANK() (ties share a rank and the next rank skips) over excess descending, partitioned by account scope
"Ranked 3 or better" means rank <= 3, which can return more than 3 pairs per scope when ties occur and may return fewer than 3 when the scope has fewer qualifying pairs

Since orderslink maps to a single order and a single user, each orderslink has exactly one account scope, so the pair is effectively one per order; alternatively, pairs are treated as distinct combinations that could differ if the join duplicates rows
Excess is the pair's average feerate minus the mean of pair averages, reported unrounded as a raw difference
Excess is expressed as a ratio or percentage over the mean rather than an absolute difference
The output columns are orderslink, acctscope, average feerate, excess, and rank, with no rounding applied, and ordering by scope then rank
Orders are joined to users by userlink = userstamp, and users with duplicate userstamp values (if any) would duplicate fee rows and affect the averages
Missing interpretations:
Pair averages are computed over each pair's non-null feerate values only, so null feerates are not treated as zero
Ties in excess are determined by exact equality of the unrounded excess values, so floating-point or decimal precision could affect which pairs share a rank
The mean of all pair averages is taken only over pairs that survive the inner joins, so pairs whose fees have no matching order or user are excluded from the mean
"Strictly above the mean" is computed against the mean over all pairs, including those later filtered out, and not against a mean recomputed after filtering
Rank is computed only among the pairs kept after the strictly-above filter, not among all pairs
The rank is applied to the excess, and since excess is a constant offset from the average, ranking by excess gives the same order as ranking by average feerate

Each pair is a distinct (orderslink, acctscope) combination, and a single orderslink could appear in more than one scope only if the users table has duplicate userstamp values with different acctscope values
If there are no pairs above the mean (for example, all averages are equal or the table is empty), the result is empty
queries:
SELECT AVG(avg_rate) FROM (SELECT f.orderslink, u.acctscope, AVG(f.feerate) AS avg_rate FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault JOIN users u ON o.userlink = u.userstamp GROUP BY f.orderslink, u.acctscope)
WITH pair_avg AS (
  SELECT u.acctscope, o.mktnote, AVG(o.notionsum) AS avg_notional
  FROM orders o
  JOIN users u ON o.userlink = u.userstamp
  GROUP BY u.acctscope, o.mktnote
)
SELECT acctscope, mktnote
FROM pair_avg
WHERE avg_notional > (SELECT AVG(avg_notional) FROM pair_avg);
WITH pair_avg AS (
  SELECT u.acctscope, o.mktnote, AVG(o.dealquote) AS avg_price
  FROM orders o
  JOIN users u ON o.userlink = u.userstamp
  GROUP BY u.acctscope, o.mktnote
)
SELECT acctscope, mktnote, avg_price,
       AVG(avg_price) OVER (PARTITION BY acctscope) AS scope_mean_avg_price
FROM pair_avg;
SELECT AVG(pair_avg) FROM (SELECT AVG(f.feerate) AS pair_avg FROM orders o JOIN fees f ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.mktnote) WHERE pair_avg IS NOT NULL
SELECT AVG(feerate) FROM fees;
SELECT u.acctscope, AVG(f.feerate) AS avg_feerate, COUNT(*) AS fee_count
FROM fees f
JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault
JOIN users u ON o.userlink = u.userstamp
GROUP BY u.acctscope;
